newsitem.title: FRANCE: Germany faces difficulty on EMU-French Socialist.
newsitem.headline: Germany faces difficulty on EMU-French Socialist.

text.p: Germany is unlikely to be readier than France to comply with a strict interpretation of the Maastricht treaty on monetary union, Socialist interim party secretary Francois Hollande said on Thursday.
"I do not have the feeling that the Germans will be much readier than us" to comply with the treaty, he told French television station LCI.

"There are no good or bad pupils. There are all those who are trying to converge," he added. "Do you or do you not want to create the euro? Are you going to refuse this because of being at 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 or even 3.4 percent?"

The Socialist government has said it is determined to launch the single currency on time on January 1, 1999. But it has urged a flexible reading of the Maastricht treaty goal of limiting public deficits to three percent of gross domestic product.

Hollande added that the Socialists' alliance with the Communist party was going well. The Socialists failed to win an absolute majority in the June 1 parliamentary election and formed a coalition government with the Communists.
"The atmosphere is good and there's total solidarity," Hollande said.
